## WORK-HC4-SCHUR

**Find or exclude a genuinely different mixed/coisotropic HC4 descent**

**Disposition:** archived-programme. **Kind:** research. **Compute class:** none.

**Next step:** For the unrestricted relative-linear unit-pivot branch, work on the output Keller pair G with certified ideal (x,y) and Jacobian -2, quotienting the complete matrix stabilizer. Prove or disprove properness at zero by determining the omitted normalization fibre of length d-1. Do not infer completeness from the singleton affine fibre. Other genuinely remaining mechanisms include base-dependent alternating dual words, nonlinear base changes, different graph charts and mixed/coisotropic pivots, with actual Hessian and collision-covector transformations. For a pencil route, supply every omitted radial divisor including e=1 terms, balance sum(e_i*f_i)=d-1, and independently reconcile genus and punctures with the nonzero fibre-deficit budget. Rationality and special-member irreducibility must be proved using actual Keller information, not row ideal equality. For a specific omitted normalization point, principalize the actual radial ideal and supply Q, e, f and the canonical vector from the full boundary. Apply the pointwise length and cyclic-chain congruence gates. A sole degree-one horizontal on an all-b>=2 resolved chain is excluded; an odd-node-style extra -1 horizontal is outside that stratum. The collided tame-node projection controls are now globally excluded by PF2BATT1; use a different finite-map germ or global boundary pattern, rather than attaching an odd-node -1 curve to repair that family. Use PF2OMIT1 and the global omitted-divisor ledger: certify the normal algebra and reconstruction ideal product(B:x_i), then list all pole primes with independent ramification/omission flags, target images, residue degrees and exceptional ambient lengths. In the two nonimmersed r7 cases enforce B(y)<=2 at every two-branch value; count normalization branches per prime even when target images coincide or self-intersect. For singleton zero require ramified local lengths plus unramified branch counts to total d-1, and exclude both kinds to establish properness. The ledger nulls are unresolved inputs, not absent primes. Apply PF2OMIT2 to the immersed r7 family as well: exactly three omitted unramified primes, at least two with images different from C. At a singleton zero outside the finite branch locus require at least two units of image branch surplus, counted per prime. Audit old whole-even conclusions against omitted e1 rows and transport the Stein model through target blowups explicitly. For an actual plane candidate, PF2OMIT3 replaces an arbitrary resolvent by a source-finite primitive inverse: certify output monicity in the complementary source coordinate and the coefficient unit ideal, factor its leading coefficient for every omission image, and use specialization degree for exact aggregate fibre lengths. The remaining immersed r7 inverse leading coefficient needs an image factor beyond the ramified curve. Individual e,f and exceptional local points still require normalized residual data; no inverse is inferred from a terminal passport alone. PF2OMIT4 separates the normalized different from squared inverse-order index factors: retain f weights and do not read primitive-coordinate collisions as ramification or lost sheets. For an off-branch singleton, require the actual inverse coefficient staircase and discriminant order>=(d-1)*(d-2); degree6 requires order20, and its single-e2f1 index factor has order>=10. The immersed r7 ledger has five generic image groupings, of which only three admit an off-branch singleton, requiring three or four nonproper target components. These are necessary constraints; the actual normalized algebra and image equations are still needed. PF2OMIT5 now excludes the entire degree6 single e2,f1 ramified-prime gap21 stratum without source finality. That closes its immersed quartic and multiple-root reciprocal continuations. Audit the entire-ramification hypothesis before applying this result to a terminal passport; unrestricted singleton-zero properness and other ramification patterns still require the complete actual normalization ledger. In a degree6 application containing an immersed e2,f1 gap21 prime, an off-branch singleton forces exactly one further e2 ramified prime with zero excess and one unramified omitted prime with a five-branch image at zero. The three nonproper target components are distinct; determine the extra ramified residue degree and both unknown image equations before claiming a complete cover or properness. PF2OMIT6 now fixes every residual r7 residue degree to1 and supplies all pointwise source-length and singleton branch rules. Determine actual image equations and the exceptional value, rather than treating f as free or continuing the single-prime reciprocal branch already excluded by PF2OMIT5. At an off-branch singleton with sole unramified pole order p, enforce leading order5p, raw discriminant order>=20p and index factor order>=10p. PF2OMIT7 fixes the residual excess-one point as a regular ordinary cusp and gives all singleton radial rows, charts, fibre lengths and canonical vectors. For an actual image B locate its unique common derivative root and require nonzero second/third jet determinant. Retain the explicit radial/strict node intersections after target blowup; only the corresponding original targetA2 projection is forbidden. Complete the global affine image equations and attachment data rather than reclassifying those resolved local algebras. PF2OMIT8 requires the actual residual image pair to support connected S6 monodromy with one2-cycle over C and one2/3-cycle over B. The source field has no proper intermediate field; a composite-degree tower or the discriminant sign double cover is not a replacement normalization. Retain the unramified omitted prime even when its distinct image has identity inertia. Candidate equations and their actual global complement relations are still required.

**Completion evidence:** A polynomial global collision or a theorem excluding the complete stated pivot stratum.

**Prerequisites and boundary:** HC4MYGALL1 closes the standard graph chart; HC4MYGT2 closes both all-degree triangular orders and arbitrary base-independent Keller substitutions. Its elementary proof HC4MYGT1 includes a positive control with one affine direction, so one must test the whole cotangent plane. Long base-independent words are not a remaining gate. Polynomially invertible parameterizations need not preserve a unit Hessian determinant. HC4MYOR1 classifies the relative-linear row orbit and full stabilizer. HC4MYOR2 supplies the normalized degree99 sufficient region; high-degree matrices can repeat the same linear map. The general singleton-zero properness gate remains open. HC4MYPP1 gives the weighted boundary and Euler budgets; HC4MYPP2 shows no genus bound follows from the oriented ideal and determinant-one row orbit, even with a fixed nonconstant Jacobian polynomial. Its controls are not Keller maps. HC4MYRB1 gives the local intersection and canonical gates and the all-length chain exclusion. HC4MYRB2 shows why a minimal surface resolution alone is insufficient and why the local normal-cover controls do not solve the global A2 attachment problem.
